item.title: What is 'DL Trade?' Slang Explained
item.description: Trade or DL Trade are slang terms that originated in African-American and LGBTQ spaces, and have since spread throughout the internet, entering common use on various social media platforms, such as Twitter / X, TikTok and Instagram.

item.title: The 'Japan Footsteps' Copypasta Evolves Into A Meme About Japanese People Charging Their Phones
item.description: People In Japan When Their Phone Dies is a series of memes, including video edits, referencing the "Japan Is Turning Footsteps Into Electricity" copypasta where a clip of someone walking is shown under a version of the caption, "People in Japan when their phone dies," the joke being that they can turn their footsteps into electricity to charge their phone. The trend was popularized on Instagram Reels and TikTok between late February and early March 2026.

item.title: Where Did This Image of Aliens Holding Hands Come From?
item.description: Aliens Holding Hands or Aliens Touching Heads refers to a reaction image and exploitable meme featuring two aliens grasping hands and leaning towards each other, as the alien on the right caresses the other alien. First posted to Tumblr sometime in 2015, the image gained renewed attention as it spread on social media platforms like X / Twitter and TikTok from 2024 into early 2026. The image is used to convey understanding and synchronicity of thought between two people.

item.title: Modern Gaming Tropes Mocked Relentlessly In 'But It's A Modern Game' Meme Trend
item.description: But It's a Modern Game or Modern Game Parodies refers to a series of video memes that apply arguably negative modern triple-A gaming tropes, primarily overly-expository tutorial narration and prompts and cheesy dialogue, to older video games. The trend was inspired by the viral Triple-A Mario video that went viral in December 2025, featuring many of the same criticisms of modern gaming. item.title: What Does 'Cortisol Spike' Mean? The Cortisol Meter Meme And Slang Explained
item.description: The High Cortisol Meme is used to humorously describe moments of sudden stress, shock and second-hand embarrassment.
